# AI Media Scout — 2026-11-22

The edition has 100 complete guides and 13 screened discoveries. It completes 23 earlier pending guides and details 7 substantive release updates. Today’s source reviews cover Kilnframe’s FilmCraft integration and Clio’s on-device FilmCraft and Whisper workflow on Android. Other guides span animated dialogue, editable stem and MIDI handoffs, and learned material capture. Models and OS requirements vary by workflow. Code grants were read in full. Models, services, creative inputs and hardware or software hosts have separate requirements. This edition is based on source review and published documentation. No discovered app was installed or run. The expanded plan covered 120 fields, 1378/1378 repository-query attempts and 37 model tasks. The repository lane recorded 1378 successful, 0 partial and 0 failed queries, with 254 bounded. The model lane recorded 0 failed tasks. Metadata from 2,864 saved repository pages included 84,512 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog spans 120,138 candidates, including pilot history and 1,080 previously screened guides still pending before this edition. Creative relevance and the complete software grant were checked before including any discovery. Unreviewed and excluded records stay in local research. Live primary research yielded 800 complete usable responses from 1022 distinct URL attempts, including a non-GitHub source in each of 120 fields. 14 captures reached the size bound and 208 other sources were inaccessible or unusable. The ecosystem checks cover all 8 configured groups and record available findings and gaps. Evidence labels in this edition are 0 Recommended, 0 Ready to try, 100 Quality unverified, 13 Experimental. Repository searches returned no saved rows for Camera-reactive projection installations, Live production accessibility and routed captions, Learned material capture and de-lighting, Learned projector compensation and exhibit color. Primary web research for these fields is included in the coverage notes. Updated evidence labels for previous entries: Hologram Parallax Photo Studio (Experimental to Quality unverified), Arm Compute Flow Bricks (Quality unverified to Experimental). 33 model tasks reached the configured response limit of 50 rows. A model record remains a discovery lead until code and use are verified. Model tasks with no rows: text2text-generation, zero-shot-audio-classification, audio-segmentation, image-matting. The separate watchlist made 67 unsuccessful repository checks. Collection logged 5 enrichment failures. Credential-shaped material in unsealed captures was removed before sealing. The affected source origins and before-and-after hashes remain in private evidence.

Documentation reviewed today. Tools are not hands-on tested unless explicitly stated. Requirements and performance remain source-specific.

## Search and review counts

120 creative fields; 1378/1378 repository queries attempted; 37/37 model-task queries attempted. 85396 distinct source candidates and 1489 model leads. 100 detailed profiles and 13 additional screened discoveries. Source gaps: 0 failed repository queries, 0 partial repository queries, 254 bounded repository queries, 0 failed model-task queries and 0 web ecosystem gaps. Raw search candidates include duplicates of known tools, excluded projects and projects awaiting review; they are not verified recommendations.

## Research beyond GitHub

- **gitlab** · searched: Current GitLab API captures include targeted subtitle and texture searches and Retell’s project and MIT terms. The maintainer describes a Mac-local caption and dub workflow. Many deeper GitLab requests returned HTTP 429. Canonical eScriptorium and Arkindex sources were also checked. 68 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. Topical subtitle, OCR and audio searches returned HTTP 429, leaving broad coverage incomplete. 15 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. [Source](https://codeberg.org/MightyOwlbear/Raspberry-Pi-5-Diffusion/raw/branch/main/README.md) [Source](https://codeberg.org/MightyOwlbear/Raspberry-Pi-5-Diffusion/raw/branch/main/LICENSE) [Source](https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/MightyOwlbear/Raspberry-Pi-5-Diffusion)

[Source](https://git.sr.ht/~rockerboo/diffuser/blob/main/LICENSE) [Source](https://git.sr.ht/~rockerboo/diffuser/blob/main/Cargo.toml) [Source](https://git.sr.ht/~rockerboo/diffuser/refs)

Package metadata informs setup, and the software license and model terms are examined separately. 5 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/pymss/2.4.0/json) [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/basic-pitch/0.4.0/json) [Source](https://pypi.org/pypi/Montreal-Forced-Aligner/3.4.4/json)
- **creative-plugins** · searched: The published Blender Lip Sync entry documents the offline model and spritesheet setup. The OBS resource for LocalVocal documents a different speech-to-caption workflow. Host and version compatibility are checked for each plugin. 8 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. - **project-sites** · searched: PyMSS Studio, Material Palette and Spotify Basic Pitch supplied official workflow or evaluation references for local stems, learned material extraction and audio-to-MIDI conversion. 3 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. [Source](https://pymss.net/en/studio/) [Source](https://astra-vision.github.io/MaterialPalette/) [Source](https://basicpitch.spotify.com/)
- **research-code** · searched: The primary Material Palette paper documents color, roughness and normal-map estimation and links the released software. The newer BTF paper describes a distinct measured-material representation. Publication alone leaves code release and licensing open. 2 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. Model terms and platform support remain separate reviews. 8 direct attempts were unavailable, access-gated or bounded. 1. Use the documented release package on a supported GPU-equipped host and confirm the editor version.

### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/erhanmeydan/kilnframe/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://kilnframe.com/plugin/) [Source 3](https://github.com/erhanmeydan/kilnframe/blob/main/docs/ilk-animasyon.md)

1. Mark a short owned passage and pick a visual style. Use the generated scene preview to check what it understood from the speech.
2. Correct words, claims and placement in the review step and render only the approved insert.
3. Inspect separate sound effects and inserted visuals in the original timeline and keep a clean duplicate for comparison.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/erhanmeydan/kilnframe/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://kilnframe.com/plugin/) [Source 3](https://github.com/erhanmeydan/kilnframe/blob/main/docs/ilk-animasyon.md)

- **Hardware:** The maintainer requires a GPU and documents an approximately 1 GB speech-model download on initial use. Minimum RAM, VRAM and disk size for all combinations are undocumented.
- **Software:** FilmCraft 0.14.0+, Premiere Pro 2026 26.2+, or DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1+, the Kilnframe panel or companion app, speech model and selected vision model.
- **Platforms:** Apple silicon macOS (M1 or later), or 64-bit Windows 10/11 according to the current package docs. Intel macOS lacks a documented release.

- **Weights:** Apache-2.0 covers Kilnframe. HyperFrames and host editor terms are separate, along with any local or cloud models. The optional Google music feature has separate terms.
- **Commercial:** Project code is governed by Apache-2.0. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
- **Cost:** Local rendering uses compute and storage. Generation can use a documented local model or a paid plan/API. Optional music uses a separately billed Google API.

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. ### Introduction

phoonnx synthesizes speech from multiple ONNX voice families with a common runtime and provides a documented offline voice cache. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

### What it is good for

Produce a draft narration WAV for an original script and check pronunciation and pacing before trimming the recorded track into a video. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

### Demo & examples

The maintainer documents downloaded voice snapshots, local synthesis examples and which model types can provide phoneme alignment output. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

### Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

1. Prepare Python 3.11 or later and a compatible ONNX Runtime. Add only the extras required by the selected voice engine and text frontend.
2. Read the voice card and download the correct artifacts before an offline session. Save the exact model and vocoder choices.
### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

1. Start with a short script and synthesize a draft WAV using a voice with documented terms.
2. Listen for unusual names, cadence and sentence boundaries. Revise the script or phoneme input as the selected voice allows.
3. Check timing against the video edit. If you need machine-readable alignment, use only a documented compatible engine and verify its timestamps.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/README.md) [Source 2](https://pypi.org/project/phoonnx/) [Source 3](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/installation.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/offline.md) [Source 5](https://github.com/TigreGotico/phoonnx/blob/dev/docs/alignment.md) [Source 6](https://huggingface.co/Phoonnx/fastpitch-en_us-ljspeech-gruut/raw/main/README.md)

### How it uses AI

The released vocoder reconstructs 16 kHz speech from learned WavLM representations via a HiFi-GAN-style decoder trained on French speech. ### How it uses AI

NeuralNote uses the MuScriptor transformer to turn music audio into editable, instrument-separated MIDI in a plug-in or standalone app. [Source](https://github.com/DamRsn/NeuralNote/blob/main/README.md) [Source](https://github.com/DamRsn/NeuralNote/releases/tag/v2.2.0) [Source](https://huggingface.co/DamRsn/muscriptor-gguf/raw/main/README.md) [Source](https://kyutai.org/blog/2026-07-10-muscriptor/)

NeuralNote uses the MuScriptor transformer to turn music audio into editable, instrument-separated MIDI in a plug-in or standalone app. Documented inputs include WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, Ogg Vorbis and, on macOS v2.2.0, M4A. ### Introduction

Spirula Studio trains Gaussian scene models from photo or video and includes learned masks and matching in its Vulkan workflow. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

### What it is good for

From a small multi-angle capture, prepare a cleaned set splat and compare distant details and mask edges across a few test views. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

### Demo & examples

The developer publishes capture-to-splat and mesh examples. The current release adds calibration-residual correction, improved floater suppression, new learned matching and new large-scene viewer behavior. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

### Install

Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

1. Use the documented package for the selected Windows, Linux or Mac GPU, or follow the Vulkan source build guide.
2. Check the camera and model requirements. Optional masking and other preprocessing weights must match the documented backend and terms.
### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

1. Start with an original photo set or supported video and inspect pose solve and masks before training.
2. Train a small batch and compare geometry, framing and distant detail on withheld views. Test the effect of calibration and revised floater suppression separately.
3. Save the trained scene and compare export render or textured mesh to the source before using it in an edit or exhibit.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

- **Hardware:** The author documents Vulkan across NVIDIA, AMD, Intel and Apple devices, and a separate legacy CUDA path. Its 8 GB demonstration claim is specific to selected training settings.
- **Software:** Windows, Linux or macOS with a compatible GPU, Spirula Studio and optional weight downloads for the selected preprocessing. Build prerequisites vary by backend.
- **Platforms:** Documented cross-platform Vulkan or MoltenVK route. Legacy CUDA on compatible NVIDIA Windows/Linux has a different feature set.

### License, model weights & costs

The full software license was reviewed. Dependencies and creative assets carry their own terms. [Source 1](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/LICENSE) [Source 2](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/README.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/build.md) [Source 4](https://github.com/harry7557558/spirula-studio/blob/master/docs/datasets.md)

- **Code:** GPL-3.0
- **Weights:** GPL-3.0 governs the application. The checked code grant is independent of optional Meta segmentation and matching weights, scene datasets and footage terms.
- **Commercial:** Project code is governed by GPL-3.0. Confirm selected model, source-media and output restrictions separately.
- **Cost:** Training can use local workstations. Scene storage, model acquisition and any explicitly chosen remote hardware are separate.

The creative workflow is grounded in the cited documentation. Output quality and compatibility are not hands-on verified. The maintainer requests investigation of any significant quality or efficiency regressions. Published settings and claims do not establish a particular production result. Follow the documented route for the scoped workflow. The steps below are source references. [Source 1](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/hardware-compatibility.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/tools-and-options.md)

1. Choose the documented platform package and check its actual local-generation compatibility table.

### First project

A small first project makes the input, model output and handoff easy to inspect. [Source 1](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/hardware-compatibility.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/tools-and-options.md)

1. Make a small edit from a rights-cleared clip and select a short replacement interval.
2. Compare rendered motion, actor or prop consistency and sound on either side of the selected range.
3. Preserve the original and approved output and document the chosen model version, clip dimensions and any effect options.
### Hardware & software

Platform and compute constraints refer to the selected route. [Source 1](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/README.md) [Source 2](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/hardware-compatibility.md) [Source 3](https://github.com/Lightricks/LTX-Desktop/blob/main/docs/tools-and-options.md)

- **Hardware:** Maintainer recommends 24 GB+ VRAM for CUDA and lists 100 GB+ free disk. Apple silicon local generation on macOS 26+ has separate unified-memory thresholds. Consult the per-tool matrix.
- **Software:** LTX Desktop and an appropriate model setup. Local LTX 2.5 Fast and 2.3 Fast are separate from API-only Pro variants. Some weights and adapters require gated access.
- **Platforms:** Windows x64, Linux x64/arm64, and Apple silicon macOS packages are documented. App installation and local generation have different OS and hardware floors.
